newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon state cotton firm preened for sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon state cotton firm preened for sell-off.

text.p: Cameroon's state cotton company SODECOTON is geared up for privatisation in June after positive 1995/96 results and government help, according to the firm's general manager.

After a record 1995/96 yield of 195,000 tonnes of cotton seed against 165,000 tonnes last year the company's belt-tightening had paid off, General Manager Mohamed Iya told a year-end national farm sector review meeting last week.
"Now it is a very attractive candidate for privatisation," he said, pointing to company profits of six million CFA in 1995/96 after going 60 billion CFA into the red last year.

Cameroon, planning 17 other privatisations this year, set seed prices artificially high for 1995/96 and picked up part of SODECOTON's debt. SODECOTON had meanwhile halved staff numbers and reduced its wage bill, Iya said.
Rising international cotton prices had restored profitability while the number of producers had leaped to 277,000 from 150,000 depite low prices in 1995/96.
Total internal prices had at one point exceeded sale prices by 450 CFA per kilo but with international prices seen firming in 1996/97 "a very discouraging period" would be over, Iya predicted.
SODECOTON is 30 percent owned the French Compagnie Francaise des Fibres but the state's 70 percent is set to be sold off by the end of June.
Domestic cotton processing capacity is rising, Cameroon's agriculture minister Frederic Kodock told the same review, without giving details.
SODECOTON also announced a turnover of 75 billion CFA, exports of 77,911 tonnes of cotton fibre and a total of 158,000 hectares under cotton producing an average of 1.23 tonnes each.
The company exports mainly to Asia with the rest for domestic consumption.
World cotton prices have suffered in recent years as man-made fibres took market share, cutting cotton's share of world textile demand.

Market analysts expect world textile demand to rise in 1997 with cotton expected to benefit. One internationally-known review has predicted an increase in world average per capita consumption to 7.24 kg in 1997 from 7.12 kg in 1995. A figure for 1996 was not available.

Cameroon's Sahelian neighbour Chad, also a cotton producer, is hoping for increased cotton export revenue. It raised its 1996/97 cotton price from 140 CFA francs per kg for top-grade seed cotton to 170 CFA to encourage production.
